result.title: Steering the Teacher: Improving On-Policy Self-Distillation for Thinking Models
result.summary: On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) trains a student on its own reasoning trajectories using token-level supervision from a reference-conditioned teacher initialized from the same model. However, access to the reference can induce teacher behaviors that undermine independent reasoning in thinking models, leading to reference hallucinations, where the student cites an unavailable reference to justify reasoning steps, and reconsideration suppression, where the teacher discourages verification and revision at uncertain steps. We introduce Steered-Teacher OPSD (ST-OPSD) to jointly address these failure modes through activation steering. ST-OPSD extracts two directions from model-generated reasoning trajectories and applies them to the teacher's hidden states during distillation target computation, suppressing reference-invoking behavior and encouraging reconsideration with marker-family calibration. The student learns from the resulting teacher distributions without being steered. Experiments on AIME and HMMT show that ST-OPSD improves accuracy over vanilla OPSD and other interventions while restoring reconsideration and reference-hallucination rates to base-model levels.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对 on-policy 自蒸馏中参考条件教师引发的两种失败模式——引用不可得参考的幻觉与抑制反思修改，提出 ST-OPSD：从模型生成的推理轨迹中提取两个激活方向，在计算蒸馏目标时作用于教师隐状态，并配合标记族校准，在 AIME、HMMT 上提升准确率并恢复反思率。
AI.relevance_reason: 「对教师隐状态做激活方向干预以重塑轨迹监督」可能为 LVR 中的轨迹训练、核查与再思考行为的塑造提供可核查线索，也可与 latent 状态中的停止决策相联系；但该工作纯文本、无视觉证据，方向提取与标记族校准能否迁移到多模态推理仍需核查。
